title: Danny Boyle backs Jack O’Connell as a potential Bond villain
body_md:
Danny Boyle has expressed support for the possibility of Jack O’Connell playing the antagonist in the next James Bond movie. In a report published on November 26, 2026, the filmmaker discussed the prospect of his Ink collaborator appearing opposite Robert Pattinson. Boyle also suggested that O’Connell would have been an excellent candidate to play 007 himself.

Speaking on the Alchemy with Anthony Mason podcast, Boyle identified a quality that he believes the two performers share. Both possess an ability to attract an audience's attention and encourage viewers to follow their characters. For the director, this is a particularly valuable characteristic because it is difficult to define or manufacture through conventional filmmaking techniques alone.

The distinction between a casting suggestion and a confirmed appointment is important. The report describes Pattinson as the actor selected to succeed Daniel Craig, while O’Connell's potential involvement is presented as a subject of discussion. Boyle's endorsement does not establish that O’Connell has signed a contract or that the filmmakers have settled on the identity of the next antagonist.

Boyle's enthusiasm for Pattinson also has a longer history. In 2019, after watching Claire Denis' science fiction film High Life, the director publicly suggested that Pattinson should become the next Bond. His latest comments indicate that he had recognized the actor's screen presence even earlier, during the Twilight films, where he also saw similar star quality in Kristen Stewart.

The director has a personal connection to the franchise. Boyle was originally attached to direct No Time to Die, Daniel Craig's final adventure as Bond, before leaving the production because of creative differences. His comments therefore come from someone who has previously considered how to approach the series, although they should not be interpreted as an official announcement from the current production team.

An encounter between Pattinson and O’Connell could offer an interesting dramatic contrast. Bond antagonists are most memorable when they challenge the protagonist's identity as well as his ability to complete a mission. Casting performers with strong individual screen presence might help create that dynamic, provided the screenplay gives both characters sufficient depth.

For now, the proposed pairing remains an intriguing possibility rather than an established feature of the upcoming film. The report does not provide a confirmed villain casting or a release date. Boyle's remarks nevertheless offer an insight into the qualities he values in actors and why he believes both men could fit into the world of James Bond.
